description:
A guard that calls a helper whose only clause head is a cons pattern panics the compiler on run when the argument's static type is not a list. interp answers correctly.

Probe:
def first([h | _]), do: h
def f(l) when first(l) > 0, do: :a
def f(_), do: :b
def main(), do: dbg([f([1]), f([]), f(7), f(:x)])

interp: [:a, :b, :b, :b]
run: panic at src/compiler2/native_codegen/value.rs:171, 'known_list_ref_for_var requires a list ref'
build: not yet run; it shares the lowering.

With a second clause def first(_), do: 0 the program compiles and runs on both paths, and so does the one-clause helper when the argument arrives through a receive (static type any). So the failing case is the helper's cons clause lowered for an activation whose argument is known not to be a list: the clause cannot match, the guard is false, and no list read should be emitted.

Seen while probing, to verify on a clean develop binary before it is treated as a second defect: the same one-clause helper in a receive guard

defp first([h | _]), do: h
receive do
  l when first(l) == 3 -> dbg(:a)
end

panics run with cranelift 'FunctionBuilder finalized, but block block8 is not filled' (binary was a worktree with unrelated uncommitted changes).

Fails before, passes after: a fixture with the probe above on interp, run and build, with an Elixir oracle; a receive-guard fixture if the second panic reproduces on develop.

Acceptance: full gate green; no pin rises.
title: A guard helper with a cons pattern, called with a value that is not a list, compiles on the native paths
